fin.title: UMass Dartmouth - Financial Information for International Undergraduate Students

test_policy.notes: UMass Dartmouth is 100% test optional for SAT/ACT. A score of 1080+ SAT or 22+ ACT (1200 SAT and 25 ACT for nursing) is encouraged because many programs are competitive.

requirements.notes: Apply with the Common App or the UMass Dartmouth application; $60 fee. International transcripts must be sealed official copies translated into English, with a minimum GPA of 2.5; 17 college-prep courses are required (4 English, 4 math, 2 foreign language, 3 lab science, 2 social science, 2 electives). Essay (up to 650 words) and a teacher/counselor letter are optional but recommended for competitive programs such as nursing, biology, engineering and psychology. Visual and Performing Arts programs require a portfolio or audition. Proof of funds of at least $54,000 (less any scholarship) is needed for the I-20.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Not required for citizens of Australia, Canada (except Quebec), the UK, Ireland, New Zealand, Guyana and English-speaking countries of Africa and the West Indies. May be waived with written verification that secondary instruction was in English, an IB curriculum, an American school, or IGCSE/O-level/GCE A-level study. Applicants below the minimums who meet all academic requirements are considered for the Gateway Program (conditional pathway).

aid.notes: Need-based aid and loans are not available to international students. All admitted international freshmen are automatically considered for a merit scholarship of $10,000-$15,500 per year with a high school GPA of 2.75+, renewable for four years while the student stays full-time with a 3.0+ cumulative GPA. The Gateway Program (English pathway, 1-2 semesters) is open to applicants with IELTS 5.0-5.5 or equivalent who meet the academic requirements.

majors.notes: Described by the university as highly competitive; priority date Mar 1, applications close May 1; SAT 1200 / ACT 25 encouraged. No seat cap is published on the pages read.
